topic: Token launchpads 2025-2026: pump.fun/PumpSwap, Zora Coins, Clanker, Doppler, Virtuals, Flaunch, Bankr, Uniswap CCA; bonding curves, graduation, LP locking, anti-sniping, fee streams, vesting, airdrops; which patterns belong inside an NFT so the holder launches tokens from their NFT account

findings.claim: pump.fun bonding curve charges 1.25% total (0.30% creator, 0.95% protocol, 0% LP); coin creation is free; graduation to PumpSwap costs 0.015 SOL; graduation is atomic and irreversible and the migrated pool is protocol-owned.
findings.relevance: Baseline fee ceiling and the 'no human step at graduation' rule.

findings.claim: PumpSwap canonical pools use a market-cap-tiered fee: creator 0.95% / protocol 0.05% / LP 0.20% at 420-1470 SOL mcap, tapering to creator 0.05% (0.30% total) at >=98,240 SOL; non-canonical pools 0.3%; creator fees apply since 13 May 2025; USDC pairing since 21 May 2026.
findings.relevance: Model for an optional market-cap-indexed creator fee schedule.

findings.claim: pump.fun lifetime revenue passed $800M by Sept 2025; 2025 gross revenue ~$971M; PumpSwap ~$11.2B volume in April 2025; graduation rate ~0.8-2% of created coins; PUMP sale July 2025 reported as $500M by some outlets and $600M by others.
findings.relevance: Scale and the fact that almost no launches graduate; numbers are secondary and partly conflicting.

findings.claim: Zora coins charge 1%: 20% LP remint, 80% market rewards split creator 62.5%/platform referral 25%/trade referral 5%/Doppler 1.25%/protocol 6.25% (= 50/20/4/1/5 of total); sniper tax decays 99%->1% over 10 seconds via fee = 99% - (elapsed/10)*(99%-1%); creator coins 1B supply with 500M vesting linearly over 5 years; content coins 10M to creator; trend coins 1 bp fee all to protocol.
findings.relevance: Reference fee split, strongest vesting signal, and a minimal effective on-chain sniper tax.

findings.claim: Zora's unified ZoraV4CoinHook (v2.3.0) uses afterInitialize (discovery + market positions via Doppler multi-curve), beforeSwap (dynamic fee incl. sniper tax) and afterSwap (collect fees, multi-hop convert to backing currency, distribute every swap); ZoraFactoryImpl exposes deploy(), deployCreatorCoin(), deployTrendCoin(), coinAddress().
findings.relevance: One hook that collects-converts-pays per swap removes claim escrow.

findings.claim: Clanker v4 = non-upgradeable Clanker factory + ClankerFeeLocker + ClankerToken plus four interfaces (IClankerLpLocker, IClankerExtensions, IClankerMevModule, IClankerHook); all implementations must be team-allowlisted; locker supports 7 reward recipients and 7 LP positions with immutable BPS; ClankerVault min lockup 7 days; ClankerAirdrop merkle with min lockup 1 day (V2 root updatable); MEV modules: 2-block delay, sniper auction on priority-ordered L2s, descending fees up to 80% decaying over max 2 minutes.
findings.relevance: The right modular shape; the allowlist and updatable roots are the parts to omit.

findings.claim: Clanker protocol fee is fixed at 20% of LP fees on top of the creator fee (1% creator -> 1.2% total; 3% -> 3.6%).
findings.relevance: Fee stacking model.

findings.claim: IClanker.deployToken(DeploymentConfig{TokenConfig, PoolConfig{hook,pairedToken,tickIfToken0IsClanker,tickSpacing,poolData}, LockerConfig{locker,rewardAdmins,rewardRecipients,rewardBps,tickLower,tickUpper,positionBps,lockerData}, MevModuleConfig, ExtensionConfig[]}) is the single launch entrypoint.
findings.relevance: Struct shape to borrow for LaunchTerms.

findings.claim: Cantina review of clanker-contracts (20 May-4 Jun 2025) found 26 issues: 6 medium (precision loss in presale distribution, incorrect protocol fee calculation, airdrop/presale incompatibility), 8 low, 8 informational, 4 gas.
findings.relevance: Extension combinations and fee math are where launchpads break.

findings.claim: Clanker: >200,000 tokens, ~$2.7B swap volume, ~$27M fees and >$13M team revenue in five months to April 2025; Farcaster acquired Clanker in Oct 2025 (secondary).
findings.relevance: Scale of EVM-side launchpads.

findings.claim: Doppler Airlock.create() validates four module states, deploys token+governance+timelock, initialises the bonding pool and migration pool and calls lockPool(migrationPool) so the destination cannot be traded early; migrate() is permissionless; protocol fee = max(fees/20, proceeds/1000) capped at fees/5 with the remainder of trading fees to the integrator; Airlock is Ownable with setModuleState.
findings.relevance: Lock-the-destination-pool pattern fixes the Four.meme/Virtuals bug class; the owner/admin is what we must not copy.

findings.claim: Doppler whitepaper (Jan 2024; Adams, Czernik, Lakhal, Zipfel): dutch-auction dynamic bonding curve with linear tick decay in log-space, tickAccumulator, bonding curve b_c(t)=gamma*(t/t_max)+tau_t, pro-rata refunds under minimum proceeds, early exit at maximum proceeds; argues for a token factory with known bytecode.
findings.relevance: Alternative price-discovery mechanism; token-factory doctrine.

findings.claim: Doppler docs: protocol takes 5% of trading fees on EVM (7.5% Solana); beneficiary fees may decay 80%->1%; StreamableFeesLocker beneficiaries sum to 1e18 with protocol owner >=5% and a lockDuration; DERC20 has vestingDuration, cliffDuration, yearlyMintRate; migrations noOp/v2/v3/v4; Doppler core is BUSL-1.1.
findings.relevance: Fee/vesting parameters and the licence question.

findings.claim: Uniswap CCA: AuctionParameters{currency,tokensRecipient,fundsRecipient,startBlock,endBlock,claimBlock,tickSpacing,validationHook,floorPrice,requiredCurrencyRaised,auctionStepsData}; submitBid(maxPriceQ96,amount,owner,prevTickPriceQ96,hookData); bids spread over the remaining schedule; uniform clearing price per checkpoint; full refund via exitBid if never graduated; IValidationHook.validate reverts to reject bids; factory v2.1.0 at 0x000000001F26a0044BaA66024e7b6599c61963F8; audited by Spearbit, OpenZeppelin, ABDK (v2.0.0 reports dated 06/16/2026); MIT.
findings.relevance: Auction mechanism we can adopt verbatim, plus the validation-hook seam for NFT gating.

findings.claim: CCA integration rules: steps are uint64 (24-bit MPS rate, 1e7=100%, + 40-bit blocks); min tick spacing 2, recommended >=1bp of floor; max supply 2^100; min floor 2^32+1; the last block must sell a significant amount or the final price is manipulable; no fee-on-transfer, no <6-decimal tokens; protocol fee controller is read at application time so an upgrade affects in-flight auctions; address(0) disables fees.
findings.relevance: Parameter validation to enforce in our launch UI/contract; mutable fee controller conflicts with immutability.

findings.claim: Uniswap Liquidity Launcher: InstantLaunchStrategy fixes 1e9*1e18 supply, native-ETH pair, 25 bps, tick spacing 60, no hook, LP NFT permanently locked in a FeeSplitter with permissionless collectFees and immutable splits; LBPStrategy reserves the pool id at registration; periphery includes TimelockedPositionRecipient, VestingClaimRecipient, MerkleClaimFactory, BeneficiaryVault (transferable ERC-721 is the fee beneficiary), BuybackAndBurnClaimRecipient; warns malicious parameters can make migration impossible and return funds to recipient.
findings.relevance: Zero-admin locked-LP custodian and an ERC-721 fee-beneficiary precedent.

findings.claim: Aztec ran the first CCA in Nov 2025 raising $60M from >17,000 bidders with no sniping or automated manipulation detected; Uniswap Auctions tab live 2 Feb 2026.
findings.relevance: Evidence that continuous clearing defeats sniping at scale.

findings.claim: CCA whitepaper (Nov 2025, Adams et al.): bids are spread across the remaining release schedule; uniform clearing each period; nests one-shot/TWAP/VWAP; risks: uniform-price auctions are not strategy-proof, poor release schedules create end-of-auction manipulation.
findings.relevance: Mechanism guarantees and limits.

findings.claim: Flaunch: 1% swap fee paid in ETH (flETH); default 80% creator / 20% community (Progressive Bid Wall: each 0.1 ETH of fees places a wall one tick below spot, moved up by a hook; or treasury); optional protocol fee 0-10% via FLAY governance as a waterfall; 30-minute fixed-price fair launch where the hook fills a position and buyers can exit at entry minus fees; flaunching fee 0.1% of configured market cap; creator revenue belongs to the holder of a revenue NFT; sniper protection is app-level CAPTCHA and per-wallet caps; 4,755 tokens on PositionManager1.
findings.relevance: Fee waterfall, fixed-price window, fee-stream-as-NFT precedent; its anti-bot layer is off-chain.

findings.claim: Virtuals: anti-sniper buy tax 99%->1% over 0s/60s/10min/98min windows (98-min preset may apply buy/sell/both); collected tax buys back the token over 24h into the team wallet with 3-month cliff + 9-month linear vest; 1% trading fee split 70% creator / 30% treasury; graduation at 42,000 VIRTUAL into Uniswap V2 with LP locked 10 years; Hyperboost releases idle supply over 14 days post-graduation; 60 Days module escrows founder fees and refunds all raised funds if the founder does not commit.
findings.relevance: Longest sniper window, 10-year LP lock, commit-or-refund trial launch.

findings.claim: Virtuals: Jan 2025 disclosure that attackers could pre-create the Uniswap V2 pair ahead of graduation, patched with a new contract; Code4rena review Apr-May 2025 with 32 unique findings; 18,000+ agents and >$8B DEX volume by early 2026.
findings.relevance: Destination-pool pre-creation bug class; scale.

findings.claim: Bankr launcher: 0.7% pool fee with 95% to creator (0.665% of volume) plus hook-added 0.285% permanently-locked compounding LP fee, 0.475% Bankr protocol fee, 0.2375% BNKR buyback, ~0.0875% Doppler (1.75% all-in); 100B supply, 85% pool / 15% creator vesting 1 year with 30-day cliff; limits 50 deploys/day, 1/min, optional 24h wallet-age anti-sybil gate; fee schedules fixed at launch and never changed retroactively.
findings.relevance: Agent-launch rate limits and an LP-compounding fee leg.

findings.claim: March 2025: Grok's token-name replies caused Bankr's bot to deploy 17 tokens; DRB peaked above $40M market cap and Grok's wallet accrued >$500k in fees; Bankr disabled Grok interactions saying Grok 'was not built to responsibly manage its own wallet'.
findings.relevance: Launch authority for agents must be scoped and revocable.

findings.claim: Cork Protocol lost $11M on 28 May 2025 because its v4 hook's beforeSwap lacked an onlyPoolManager check; the attacker called it directly with a fake pool and crafted hook data.
findings.relevance: Every hook callback must verify msg.sender and the PoolKey.

findings.claim: GemPad lost $1.8M on 17 Dec 2024 via reentrancy in GemPadLock.collectFees(): Uniswap collect() triggered a malicious token transfer that re-entered multipleLock(); no nonReentrant, accounting after external calls.
findings.relevance: LP-locker security rules.

findings.claim: Four.meme (BNB Chain) lost ~$183k in Feb 2025 (attacker pre-created the PancakeSwap pair at a wrong price before migration) and ~$120-130k in Mar 2025 (migration transaction leaked and sandwiched); LIBRA (Feb 14 2025) saw ~$107M extracted by insiders sniping Meteora pools; the 'Base is for everyone' Zora coin (Apr 2025) hit ~$17M and fell >90% after three wallets front-ran the announcement; Bunni lost ~$8.4M (Sep 2025) to a rounding bug in its v4 hook.
findings.relevance: Migration front-running, insider sniping, announcement front-running and rounding are the recurring failure modes; all secondary reporting.

findings.claim: pump.fun's May 2024 ~$1.9M exploit was a former employee abusing a withdraw authority with flash loans to force curves to graduation; a RICO class action (Burwick Law) against pump.fun/Solana entities was filed Jan 2025 and expanded in July 2025; Jito defendants dismissed Sept 2025 with leave to amend.
findings.relevance: No privileged withdraw authority; legal exposure of launchpad operators.

findings.claim: ERC-7641 Intrinsic RevShare Token (Draft, created 2024-02-28; authors Conway, Cathie So, Xiaohang Yu, Suning Yao, Kartin) defines snapshot(), claimableRevenue(), claim(), redeemableOnBurn(), burn() so tokens can be burned for a pro-rata share of a revenue pool.
findings.relevance: Standard underlying ANIMA's AgentToken redemption floor; target for the sniper-tax-raises-the-floor idea.

findings.claim: Doppler reportedly powers >90% of new DEX pool launches on Base with ~40,000 asset creations per day and >$1B cumulative volume, integrated by Zora, Base App, Paragraph and Bankr; $9M seed (Q2 2025); native Solana rebuild early 2026.
findings.relevance: Doppler is the de facto EVM launch substrate; secondary numbers.

findings.claim: Local repos already contain: Kiln.sol (fixed-supply ownerless Coin, CREATE2 with launcher-mixed salt, on-chain hook-address mining `mine` view, deployHook flag check), Facet.sol (dynamic-fee hook that refuses beforeSwapReturnDelta), ANIMA AgentLaunchpad (fair window with per-address cap, snipe tax <=9900 bps decaying, fees into AgentToken redemption treasury, lpRecipient and deployer fixed at creation, atomic graduate), MASTER-NFT-PROJECT integrations/official-launch (CCA v2.1.0 + Liquidity Launcher + Doppler hash-pinned with Anvil lifecycle tests; notes BUSL question), Pixel-Garden LaunchpadCartridge/LaunchToken/VestingSales.
findings.relevance: The unified design should compose these rather than rebuild.

recommendations.recommendation: Make the NFT the signer of every launch and the owner of every fee stream: launches authorised only by the token owner or its ERC-6551 account (never renters), all creator fees paid to the token's account, and authority revoked on sale via the existing transfer hook.
recommendations.rationale: Flaunch's revenue NFT and Uniswap's BeneficiaryVault prove the fee stream is the asset; binding it to our NFT is the feature no external launchpad can offer. Sources: docs.flaunch.gg, Uniswap liquidity-launcher TechnicalReference, Kiln.mayActAs, ANIMA _update.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep a fixed-supply, ownerless token from a known factory with deterministic CREATE2 addresses and pre-send address prediction; no mint, pause, blacklist, tax or upgrade.
recommendations.rationale: Doppler's whitepaper, Clanker's non-mintable supply and Kiln's existing Coin all agree; it removes the entire 'rug lever' class. Sources: doppler.lol/whitepaper.pdf, pool.fans/clank, Kiln.sol.

recommendations.recommendation: Initialise the Uniswap v4 pool keyed to our own hook in the launch transaction and send the LP position to an immutable zero-admin custodian with permissionless fee collection (nonReentrant, effects-before-interactions); record the custodian in the launch struct.
recommendations.rationale: Pre-created destination pools cost Four.meme and nearly Virtuals; GemPad's locker fell to reentrancy; Uniswap's FeeSplitter and Doppler's lockPool show the fix. Sources: Airlock.sol, liquidity-launcher TechnicalReference, decurity.io GemPad.

recommendations.recommendation: Ship on-chain anti-sniping: decaying launch fee in beforeSwap (start <=9900 bps, default decay 2 min, max 98 min), optional 2-block no-swap delay, and route the tax to locked liquidity or the token's redemption treasury, never to the launcher.
recommendations.rationale: Zora (10 s), Clanker (<=2 min) and Virtuals (<=98 min) show decaying fees work; Virtuals routing the tax to the team wallet is extractive; Flaunch's CAPTCHA needs a server we do not have. Sources: docs.zora.co rewards, clanker gitbook v4, virtuals anti-sniper page.

recommendations.recommendation: Enforce hook hygiene as tested invariants: msg.sender == PoolManager on every callback, PoolKey validated against the launch record, address permission bits checked after deploy, no beforeSwapReturnDelta, rounding in the pool's favour with round-trip fuzzing.
recommendations.rationale: Cork ($11M) was a missing onlyPoolManager; Bunni ($8.4M) was rounding; Facet already refuses return-delta hooks. Sources: dedaub.com Cork, halborn Bunni, Facet.sol.

recommendations.recommendation: Fix the fee schedule per launch at creation (immutable BPS, total <=1.25%, creator/locked-LP/protocol legs, recipient addresses changeable only by the NFT).
recommendations.rationale: Industry centre is 1% (Zora, Flaunch, Virtuals, Clanker creator leg), pump.fun caps at 1.25%; Bankr's 'fixed at launch, never retroactive' and Clanker's immutable-BPS pattern are the right precedents; CCA's mutable fee controller is the anti-pattern. Sources: pump.fun/docs/fees, docs.bankr.bot, clanker creator-rewards page, CCA technical docs.

recommendations.recommendation: Scope agent launch authority: session keys limited to the launch selector with expiry and spend cap, quote restricted to ETH/USDC, per-NFT rate limits (1 per block, N per day).
recommendations.rationale: Bankr's Grok incident (17 unintended tokens) is exactly an unscoped bot; Bankr now rate-limits 1/min and 50/day. Sources: theblock.co Grok article, docs.bankr.bot.

recommendations.recommendation: Graduate atomically at the curve's or auction's own final price; never read spot and never recompute the curve per trade.
recommendations.rationale: pump.fun and ANIMA graduate atomically; CCA seeds at the clearing price; Four.meme's sandwiched migration and IPSEITY's own per-trade-curve bug show the alternative. Sources: pump.fun/docs/bonding-curve, CCA README, AgentLaunchpad.graduate.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer three mechanisms behind one deployer seam: instant single-sided v4 pool, bonding curve, and Uniswap CCA (own factory with address(0) or an immutable fee controller), enforcing CCA's parameter rules in UI and contract.
recommendations.rationale: MASTER-NFT-PROJECT already pins CCA v2.1.0 (MIT) with lifecycle tests; CCA is the only mechanism with a documented $60M no-sniping launch; its integration rules are explicit. Sources: Uniswap CCA README/technical docs, integrations/official-launch README.

recommendations.recommendation: Implement an NFT-gated IValidationHook for CCA bids (holder or authorised account, per-NFT caps, ERC-165 per CIP-1).
recommendations.rationale: The validation-hook seam exists precisely for eligibility; a scarce NFT is a stronger sybil barrier than CAPTCHA or wallet age. Sources: CCA README validation hooks section.

recommendations.recommendation: Add a creator vault with vesting visible before the first buy (<=15% allocation, >=30-day cliff, >=1 year linear; min lockup 7 days) and reuse Pixel-Garden's VestingSales for pre-authorised exits.
recommendations.rationale: Zora (5 y), Bankr (1 y / 30 d cliff), Virtuals (3 m cliff / 9 m) and Clanker (>=7 d) converge on vesting as the main insider defence after LIBRA. Sources: support.zora.co allocation article, docs.bankr.bot, clanker gitbook v4, Pixel-Garden VESTING-SALES.md.

recommendations.recommendation: Merkle airdrops with an immutable root, >=1-day lockup and optional linear vest; unclaimed tokens sweep to the pool or treasury, never to the launcher.
recommendations.rationale: Clanker v4.0 semantics are sound; AirdropV2's updatable root and MerkleClaim's owner withdrawal are trust assumptions we should not carry. Sources: clanker gitbook v4, liquidity-launcher TechnicalReference.

recommendations.recommendation: Offer an optional market-cap-indexed creator fee schedule (high creator share for small caps, tapering to ~0.05% with a constant LP leg) stored in the launch struct.
recommendations.rationale: pump.fun's tiered schedule (0.95% -> 0.05%, LP 0.20%) rewards early builders without taxing mature markets. Source: pump.fun/docs/fees.

recommendations.recommendation: Trial launches: escrow creator fees until commit(); on abandon or deadline route escrow and unsold supply to a pro-rata refund pool enforced by the token contract.
recommendations.rationale: Virtuals' 60 Days module shows demand for reversible launches; our version needs no governance. Source: whitepaper.virtuals.io 60 Days page.

recommendations.recommendation: Optional progressive bid wall funded by the community fee share, and a 14-day post-graduation volume reward from unsold supply measured in afterSwap.
recommendations.rationale: Flaunch's PBW and Virtuals' Hyperboost are proven retention mechanics that can run fully on-chain. Sources: flaunchgg-contracts README, virtuals launch mechanics page.

recommendations.recommendation: Same-address tokens across the five id-band chains via salts bound to chain+kernel+id; optional referral legs in the fee split.
recommendations.rationale: Clanker's super-chain token and Uniswap's USUPERC20 factory show the pattern; Zora's referral legs let third-party front ends route to our pools. Sources: clanker gitbook v4, liquidity-launcher TechnicalReference, docs.zora.co rewards.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not adopt team-allowlisted module registries, upgradeable fee controllers, LP burning, off-chain anti-bot, points airdrops, fee-on-transfer/rebasing quotes, spot-priced migration, or sniper tax paid to the launcher; do not ship Doppler core without resolving BUSL-1.1.
recommendations.rationale: Each contradicts the no-admin diamond doctrine or reproduces a documented failure; Doppler's licence is already flagged in the local integration README. Sources: clanker gitbook v4, Airlock.sol, CCA technical docs, integrations/official-launch README.

special_ideas: The NFT is the KYC: an NFT-gated CCA validation hook with per-NFT bid caps turns a 4,096-piece edition into the sybil barrier Aztec needed ZK Passport for.
Sniper tax raises the floor: route the decaying launch tax into the token's ERC-7641-style redemption treasury so every bot that snipes raises every holder's redeemable floor.
Sell the NFT, sell the streams: all launch fee streams pay the token's account and transfer with one ERC-721 transfer, with prior authority revoked automatically by the existing transfer hook.
Bonded launches: the launcher's slashable bond (ANIMA BondVault) is first-loss collateral for launch terms, readable by buyers before they buy.
The artwork prices the launch: derive the decaying launch fee curve from IPSEITY's orientation word, as Facet already derives the pool fee.
Launch rooms in Parley: the announcement and pool initialisation are the same transaction, closing the announce-then-front-run window seen with 'Base is for everyone'.
On-chain hook recipes: use Kiln's `mine` view so the server-less page can deploy three audited recipes (decaying fee, fixed-price window, bid wall).
Commit-or-refund trials with no governance: escrowed fees and a pro-rata refund pool enforced by the token contract (Virtuals 60 Days without the platform).
Same token address on all five id-band chains via salts bound to chain + kernel + id (Pixel-Garden deploymentSalt).
Self-custodial automated capital formation: Pixel-Garden's beneficiary-authorised VestingSales as a keeper-less version of Virtuals' limit-sell ACF.
open_questions: Doppler is BUSL-1.1 while CCA and the Liquidity Launcher are MIT: ship Doppler at all, or only CCA plus our own curve?
CCA's protocol fee controller is mutable mid-auction when governance-owned: deploy our own factory with address(0) or an immutable controller, and does that forfeit canonical addresses?
Which chains in our id bands have Cancun, a v4 PoolManager and priority ordering (Clanker's sniper auction only works on priority-ordered L2s)?
Can the CCA bid-book UI (tick linked list, checkpoints, >2,048-hop partial-exit hints) be served from chain within EIP-170 page limits, and at what size cost given MASTER-NFT-PROJECT's existing desk?
Quote currencies: ETH only, or ETH + USDC (pump.fun added USDC May 2026; CCA recommends the currency be more valuable than the token)?
Target total fee: 1.00% (Zora/Flaunch/Virtuals) or 1.25% (pump.fun curve), and is a Bankr-style 0.285% LP-compounding leg worth its gas on L2?
With ~1-2% graduation rates industry-wide, should each NFT be bounded to N live launches so the on-chain registry stays readable without an indexer?
Legal framing: what on-chain disclaimer does the site render (Zora/Coinbase: 'collectibles, not investments'; pump.fun faces a RICO suit), and does the protocol ever promote a specific launch?
Should an agent's first launch require a human guardian co-signature (the Grok lesson)?
Several headline numbers (Clanker $5.0B/$49.7M, Zora $376M/$27.7M, Flaunch $75M, PUMP sale $500M vs $600M) are secondary or conflicting and must be re-measured before appearing in our docs.
